{{Short description|American executive}}

'''Judy Gradwohl''' is an American non-profit executive who serves as president and CEO of the [[San Diego Natural History Museum]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-04-05 |title=Natural History Museum names new president |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2016/04/05/natural-history-museum-names-new-president/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241006201712/https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2016/04/05/natural-history-museum-names-new-president/ |archive-date=2024-10-06 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=San Diego Union-Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2016, Gradwohl became the first woman to serve in this role in the museum's 150-year history. During her tenure, the museum has transitioned from traveling to in-house exhibitions, shifted its strategic focus toward applied conservation research, and developed new curricula blending onsite, online, and nature-based activities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Judy Gradwohl: President and CEO |url=https://www.sdnhm.org/about-us/judy-gradwohl/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241006202349/https://www.sdnhm.org/about-us/judy-gradwohl/ |archive-date=2024-10-06 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=The Nat |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Shulman |first=Ron |date=2021-09-09 |title=Someone San Diego Should Know: Judy Gradwohl |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2021/09/09/someone-san-diego-should-know-judy-gradwohl/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241006203118/https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2021/09/09/someone-san-diego-should-know-judy-gradwohl/ |archive-date=2024-10-06 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=San Diego Union-Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

Under Gradwohl's leadership, the museum received an $800,000 grant in 2024 from the [[Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation]] to launch a statewide initiative to coordinate and enhance environmental equity research in California's three major urban centers by promoting [[citizen science]], in which residents are invited to contribute to data collection and analysis.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2024-01-13 |title=The Nat Awarded $800K to Create Urban Nature Alliance with L.A., Bay Area Groups |url=https://timesofsandiego.com/arts/2024/01/12/the-nat-awarded-800k-to-create-urban-nature-alliance-with-l-a-bay-area-groups/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240112222723/https://timesofsandiego.com/arts/2024/01/12/the-nat-awarded-800k-to-create-urban-nature-alliance-with-l-a-bay-area-groups/ |archive-date=2024-01-12 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=Times of San Diego |language=en-US}}</ref> Partners include the [[Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County]], San Francisco's [[California Academy of Sciences]], and the [[University of California, Berkeley]].

==Education==
Gradwohl attended the University of California, Berkeley, where she received an undergraduate fellowship to study the behavior of tropical birds at the [[Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute]] on [[Barro Colorado Island]] in Panama.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Judy Gradwohl - Field notes, 1978-1979 for project 17150 {{!}} Smithsonian Digital Volunteers |url=https://transcription.si.edu/project/17150 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108024241/https://transcription.si.edu/project/17150 |archive-date=2021-01-08 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=transcription.si.edu}}</ref> This research served the basis of both her bachelor's and master's degrees in zoology.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Magazine |first=SD Metro |date=2016-04-05 |title=Natural History Museum Chooses Smithsonian Veteran as New CEO |url=https://www.sandiegometro.com/2016/04/daily-business-report-april-5-2016/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241006204937/https://www.sandiegometro.com/2016/04/daily-business-report-april-5-2016/ |archive-date=2024-10-06 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=SD METRO |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Career ==
Beginning her career at the [[National Zoological Park (United States)|National Zoo]], Gradwohl served in a number of different roles at the [[Smithsonian Institution]] from 1985 to 2016, eventually becoming the MacMillan Associate Director for Education and Public Engagement at the [[National Museum of American History]]. In addition to curating major traveling exhibits on tropical forest and ocean conservation, she was responsible for developing the Smithsonian's first website<ref>{{Cite web |date=2004-03-03 |title=Visiting the Virtual Museum |url=https://www.commarts.com/features/visiting-the-virtual-museum |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241006211906/https://www.commarts.com/features/visiting-the-virtual-museum |archive-date=2024-10-06 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=Communication Arts |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wright |first=Jennifer |date=2015-05-07 |title=The Electronic Smithsonian |url=https://siarchives.si.edu/blog/electronic-smithsonian |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240930103029/https://siarchives.si.edu/blog/electronic-smithsonian#expand |archive-date=2024-09-30 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=Smithsonian Institution Archives}}</ref> and establishing its Office of Environmental Awareness.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Niekrasz |first=Emily |date=2019-05-22 |title=Wonderful Women Wednesday: Judy Gradwohl |url=https://siarchives.si.edu/blog/wonderful-women-wednesday-judy-gradwohl |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240619064540/https://siarchives.si.edu/blog/wonderful-women-wednesday-judy-gradwohl#expand |archive-date=2024-06-19 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=Smithsonian Institution Archives |language=en}}</ref>

Gradwohl is an alumna of the [[Museum Leadership Institute at Claremont Graduate University]] and the Noyce Leadership Institute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gradwohl, Judy |url=https://mli.cgu.edu/gradwohl-judy/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240709014459/https://mli.cgu.edu/gradwohl-judy/ |archive-date=2024-07-09 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=The Museum Leadership Institute |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2018, she was the recipient of a fellowship to attend [[Harvard Business School]]'s “Strategic Perspectives in Nonprofit Management” executive education program.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 5, 2024 |title=Fellowships |url=https://www.hbssandiego.org/s/1738/cc/21/page.aspx?sid=1738&gid=75&pgid=44712 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241006210513/https://www.hbssandiego.org/s/1738/cc/21/page.aspx?sid=1738&gid=75&pgid=44712 |archive-date=2024-10-06 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=Harvard Business School}}</ref> From 2020 to 2023, Gradwohl served on the [[Aspen Institute]]'s Science & Society Program Advisory Council.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Science & Society Program Advisory Council |url=https://www.aspeninstitute.org/programs/science-society/advisory-council/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201001234048/https://www.aspeninstitute.org/programs/science-society/advisory-council/ |archive-date=2020-10-01 |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=The Aspen Institute |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Books ===
Gradwohl, J. and R. Greenberg. (1988). ''Saving the Tropical Forests''. Earthscan, London, UK. 

Gradwohl, J. (1988). ''Tropical Rainforests:  A Disappearing Treasure''. Smithsonian Institution, Washington, DC. 

Weber, M.L. and J.A. Gradwohl. (1995). ''The Wealth of Oceans:  Environment and Development on Our Ocean Planet''. W.W. Norton & Company, New York. 

Benchley, P. and J. Gradwohl. (1995). ''Ocean Planet:  Writings and Images of the Sea''. Smithsonian Institution, Washington, DC.
